content: The Egyptian blood transfusion system involves multiple stakeholders who are responsible for the provision of blood and blood components across the country. However, the data presented in this report is limited to the National Blood Transfusion Services (NBTS), which operates 24 regional blood banks covering most of Egypt's governorates. Blood units collected from hospital-based blood banks, amounting to 6% of the total, are not included in this report. The French blood establishment consists of 17 regional facilities, along with an army blood center (CTSA), whose data is integrated into this report to the extent possible. Estimates regarding blood services were derived from responses provided by hospital-based blood centers. However, some hospital-based blood centers, contributing an estimated 10% of the data, are not covered in this report. Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) Belgium collects approximately 1,000 blood units annually. In Luxembourg, the Oncology-Haematology Department of the Centre Hospitalier du Luxembourg performs around 250 directed platelet apheresis donations per year. In Malawi, the Malawi Blood Transfusion Service (MBTS) provides 55% of transfused units, while hospital-based blood banks supply 45%. However, only 36% of hospitals submitted complete data in 2012. In Kenya, the Kenya National Blood Transfusion Service (KNBTS) collects about 158,000 units of blood annually, which accounts for roughly 50% of the national requirement. In South Africa, blood services are delivered by two independent organizations: the South African National Blood Service (SANBS) and the Western Province Blood Transfusion Service (WPBTS). This report provides a national summary of their activities. In Turkey, the total number of blood and blood components collected in 2011 from all blood centers, including hospital-based centers, was 2,182,394 units. However, data from hospital-based transfusion centers are not included in this report. Military hospitals contribute approximately 3% of the national blood collection. In remote areas without blood centers, some hospitals collect blood from relatives of patients during emergencies. These donations are not included in the report. Additionally, inaccessibility due to insecurity in certain regions prevents data collection from transfusion centers in those areas. In Singapore, 2% of blood donations are collected by the Blood Services Group, while 7% are collected by the same group in other contexts. In the United States, the report covers the market share of major blood services, including the American Red Cross, Blood System Inc., and the New York Blood Center. In summary, the data presented in this report highlights the variability in blood collection and reporting practices across different countries and regions, with significant gaps in data coverage due to logistical, operational, and security challenges.
